newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens wins India mobile phone orders.
newsitem.headline: Siemens wins India mobile phone orders.

text.p: German industrial group Siemens AG has won orders worth 300 million marks to build five mobile phone systems in India, the company said on Monday.

Siemens' Public Communications Networks Groups are installing three systems for Aircel Digilink Pvt. which will begin service by the end of the year. Two others, for Modicom Network Pvt. Ltd., are to begin operating in February.
All five orders are for complete systems including switching equipment, Siemens GSM handsets and radio relay systems from Italtel, the joint venture between Siemens and Italy's STET.
Siemens will also supply and maintain the systems' mobile radio towers, the company said. For Aircel, Siemens is also supplying radio base stations.
Aircel, a joint venture between India's Essar Group and Swiss Telecom PTT, will use the systems to provide digital mobile phone service to the Rajasthan, Haryana and Utter Pradesh East areas.
ModiCom, a venture between India's Modi Group and Distacom Group of Hong Kong, is setting up GSM systems in the Punjab and Karnataka regions.
